CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of trafficking from health disorders they suffer.
15. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of trafficking from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officials which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint service, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation;

repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unity of tradition and etiquette of social life of the Hindu community passed down through generations in the bond of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa that has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Desa is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, local community interests based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

CHAPTER IV

AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITY

Article 5

1. The Regional Government has the authority and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
2. The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. service activities for women and children victims of violence;
b. monitoring, strengthening of victims of violence; c. capacity building of apparatus and other stakeholders.

Article 3

The objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. to protect women and children victims of violence;
b. to provide services to women and children victims of violence; andc. empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER VIII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 13

1. The Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

Article 14

1. Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of relevant SKPDs on a regular basis.
2. Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TABANAN REGENCY

NUMBER 11 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; andc. legal certainty.

CHAPTER XII

FUNDING

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other lawful sources.

Article 15

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children is conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children are used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

REGENT OF TABANAN

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

REGENT OF TABANAN

PROVINCE OF BALI

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TABANAN REGENCY

NUMBER 11 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 16

1. The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of the MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence and submitting it to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
2. Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures and form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 18

The Regent conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of the MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the region.

Article 16

Sufficiently clear

Article 20

Sufficiently clear

CHAPTER VII

SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSES

Article 12

1. The Regional Government is obligated to establish a Social Protection House and/or Safe House or other designation.
2. The Social Protection House and/or Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) shall guarantee the implementation of health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation, and social reintegration.
3. For the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the regional government may utilize social protection houses and/or safe houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

ELUCIDATION

NUMBER 11 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other lawful sources.

2. Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures and form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; andc. legal certainty.

1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of trafficking from health disorders they suffer.
15. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of trafficking from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officials which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint service, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation;

repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unity of tradition and etiquette of social life of the Hindu community passed down through generations in the bond of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa that has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Desa is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, local community interests based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

CHAPTER IV

AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITY

Article 5

1. The Regional Government has the authority and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
2. The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. service activities for women and children victims of violence;
b. monitoring, strengthening of victims of violence; c. capacity building of apparatus and other stakeholders.

Article 3

The objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. to protect women and children victims of violence;
b. to provide services to women and children victims of violence; andc. empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TABANAN REGENCY

NUMBER 11 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

Article 18

The Regent conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of the MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the region.

CHAPTER XII

FUNDING

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other lawful sources.

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; andc. legal certainty.

CHAPTER VII

SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSES

Article 12

1. The Regional Government is obligated to establish a Social Protection House and/or Safe House or other designation.
2. The Social Protection House and/or Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) shall guarantee the implementation of health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation, and social reintegration.
3. For the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the regional government may utilize social protection houses and/or safe houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

Article 14

1. Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of relevant SKPDs on a regular basis.
2. Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

CHAPTER VIII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 13

1. The Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 16

1. The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of the MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence and submitting it to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
2. Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures and form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

NUMBER 11 OF 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.

24. PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

b. non-discrimination; andc. legal certainty.

FUNDING

Article 20

The provision of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; andb. other lawful sources.

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

9. 10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of trafficking from health disorders they suffer.
15. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
16. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of trafficking from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officials which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint service, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation;

repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unity of tradition and etiquette of social life of the Hindu community passed down through generations in the bond of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa that has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Desa is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, local community interests based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.

9. 10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by assistants, law enforcement officials which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.

repatriation; social reintegration, and legal aid. 21. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.

22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unity of tradition and etiquette of social life of the Hindu community passed down through generations in the bond of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa that has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Desa is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, local community interests based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, upheld and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, welfare and justice for women and children.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not received adequate services so that minimum services are needed for victims of violence.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

CHAPTER VII

SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSES

Article 12

1. The Regional Government is obligated to establish a Social Protection House and/or Safe House or other designation.
2. The Social Protection House and/or Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) shall guarantee the implementation of health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation, and social reintegration.
3. For the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the regional government may utilize social protection houses and/or safe houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

Article 14

1. Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of relevant SKPDs on a regular basis.
2. Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 16

1. The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of the MSS for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence and submitting it to the Governor with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
2. Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
3. Further provisions regarding the procedures and form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

The principles of organizing protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; andc. legal certainty.

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.
